newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht stronger late, interbank rate down.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht stronger late, interbank rate down.

text.p: The Thai baht was higher against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday as the U.S. unit's sharp fall abroad help erase early baht losses, dealers said.
The baht was sold for the dollar in early trade after Standard and Poors downgraded the credit rating of two major commercial banks, dealers said.
"There was some baht selling against the dollar in the morning. But the dollar's slide against the yen instead triggered dollar selling," said one dealer at a foreign banks.
The baht was traded at 25.940/25.950 to the dollar near the close from 25.957/25.962 early, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate unchanged at 25.97 per dollar.
The overnight interbank rate eased further to 9.00-9.50 percent late from 9.50-10.00 in the morning on rising liquidity, dealers said.
"Dollar selling helped raise banking liquidity in the afternoon. Most banks also have enough funds to meet the reserve requirement later this week," said one money market dealer.
All commercial banks have to meet the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of every month.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was at 10.50/11.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 10.25/10.75 earlier.
